summary: Builds a three-year commissioning portfolio of skills and experiential opportunities beyond the course, using annual thematic workpackages and an accumulating evergreen asset base to grow both student reach and depth.
detailSummary:
King’s Edge will build a three-year beyond-course commissioning portfolio, growing annual mobilisation investment from £150,000 in Year 1 to £200,000 in Year 2 and £250,000 in Year 3 before moving to an indicative £175,000 annual business-as-usual requirement. The working ambition is to grow distinct student reach from at least 2,500 in Year 1, around 6% of the current King’s student population, to 4,000 in Year 2 and 6,500 in Year 3, before reaching around 9,000 students, approximately 20% of the current population, at steady state. Student-hours are expected to grow more steeply, from approximately 26,500 to 33,500 in Year 1, to 55,000 to 65,000 in Year 2, 100,000 to 115,000 in Year 3 and around 145,000 to 165,000 at steady state. Sustained high-intensity provision grows from around 350 places to 500 and then 600, before plateauing at around 600.

Each annual portfolio translates the overarching investment, reach and engagement ambition into a small number of thematic workpackages. Each workpackage receives a defined investment envelope and devolved responsibility for contributing to the portfolio’s reach, student-hours and depth ambitions. The thematic mix can evolve from year to year as student need, strategic priorities and evidence change, while 2.2.4 retains accountability for the overall investment envelope, deduplicated student reach and the balance between scalable, active and intensive provision.

The scaling model uses three complementary delivery modes. Scalable evergreen opportunities create reusable entry points, including skills courses, self-directed provision and repeatable projects, that can reach increasing numbers of students at relatively low marginal cost. Short active experiences turn that reach into meaningful participation through challenges, workshops, sprints, sandpits and other formats in which students practise, make or contribute. Sustained intensive opportunities provide the deepest forms of experiential learning through projects, placements, mentoring and comparable longer experiences. This high-touch layer is deliberately capacity-limited and grows to a viable plateau rather than being expected to scale indefinitely. As the evergreen asset base accumulates, reach and student-hours can grow faster than annual expenditure.

Year 1 is the first mapped instance of this annual commissioning model. A £150,000 portfolio is devolved across four thematic workpackages: Final-Year Career Enhancement (£50,000), Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Experience (£40,000), Belonging and Connection (£30,000), and Service and Community-Engaged Experience (£30,000). Together they carry devolved responsibility for delivering against the Year 1 portfolio ambition of at least 2,500 deduplicated distinct students, approximately 26,500 to 33,500 student-hours and around 350 sustained high-intensity places. Package-level reach intentionally sums above the portfolio target because students may participate in more than one workpackage.

Early commissioning responds to known priorities and concrete gaps in the student experience, including graduate futures, entrepreneurship, service and community engagement, belonging and participation. Over time, the thematic portfolio will become increasingly informed by external and future-facing insight, the experiential learning North Star and, as King’s Canvas matures, richer evidence about student purpose and demand. Commissioned provision should give students something meaningful to practise, contribute, produce or carry forward. Alongside curriculum-embedded opportunity growth through 2.1.4, this gives King’s Edge a direct mechanism for creating additional supply where existing provision is insufficient or uneven.
problemSolved: King’s lacks a coherent mechanism for turning identified student need, strategic priorities and evidence about future relevance into funded beyond-course provision at scale. As a result, opportunity supply is uneven, gaps can persist, and access to meaningful skills and experience can depend too heavily on local capacity, historic provision or student confidence and networks.
whatChanges: King’s Edge establishes a standing annual commissioning model that converts identified need into funded, substantive beyond-course opportunities. Each year, overarching investment, reach and engagement ambitions are devolved through thematic workpackages with defined contributions, while 2.2.4 retains portfolio-level accountability. A three-year mobilisation investment of £150,000, £200,000 and £250,000 progressively builds reusable evergreen provision, short active opportunities and sustained intensive capacity. At steady state, an indicative £175,000 annual investment sustains and refreshes the accumulated asset base, with an ambition to reach around 9,000 students, approximately 20% of the current King’s student population, while maintaining around 600 sustained high-intensity places.

caseForChange.problem:
King’s has a rich but uneven ecology of opportunities beyond the curriculum, but it does not yet have a coherent mechanism for turning evidence about student need, strategic priorities and future relevance into funded provision at scale.

Different parts of King’s can identify gaps, emerging needs and valuable forms of experience, but these do not consistently translate into a coordinated portfolio of opportunities for students. Provision can depend on local capacity, historic activity or individual initiative, with limited ability to balance reach, depth, access and strategic value across the institution.

Without a deliberate commissioning route, King’s Edge risks becoming better at understanding what students need and helping them navigate what already exists, without creating enough new supply where meaningful gaps remain.
caseForChange.opportunity:
King’s can establish a standing annual commissioning capability that converts emerging requirements from across King’s Edge into a balanced portfolio of substantive skills and experiential opportunities beyond the course.

Each year, portfolio-level ambitions can be devolved through a small number of thematic workpackages, giving accountable owners clear investment envelopes and contributions to reach, student-hours and depth while allowing the thematic mix to evolve as evidence changes. Investment can be balanced across three complementary modes: reusable evergreen provision that creates scalable entry points, short active experiences that turn reach into meaningful participation, and sustained intensive opportunities that protect depth. By accumulating high-quality evergreen courses and projects over successive years, the portfolio can increase student reach and student-hours faster than annual expenditure while continuing to protect the people-intensive experiences that cannot scale in the same way.

Over time, commissioning can become increasingly informed by student purpose and demand, external and future-facing insight, participation needs and the developing experiential learning North Star. This gives King’s a practical mechanism for growing provision where evidence suggests it will add most value.
caseForChange.whyNow:
King’s Edge is moving from proposition into mobilisation. Several parts of the programme are beginning to create concrete requirements for new opportunities beyond the curriculum, while richer sources of demand intelligence will come online progressively rather than all at once.

There is therefore a need to begin commissioning now against clear early priorities, while building a model capable of becoming more evidence-led as external validation, the experiential learning framework and King’s Canvas mature.

The immediate graduate futures context also creates a strong case for action. Students need access to substantive skills and experiences that strengthen their ability to move into the futures they want, particularly where existing graduate pathways or access to opportunity are less assured.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
King’s develops a repeatable annual way of turning student need, strategic priorities and evidence about future relevance into funded opportunities beyond the course. Portfolio ambitions are set centrally and delivered through thematic workpackages with devolved responsibility for defined contributions to investment, reach, student-hours and depth.

A managed portfolio of reusable evergreen, short active and sustained intensive provision gives students access to meaningful skills development and experience. Successive mobilisation years build both annual opportunity supply and an accumulating asset base, allowing more students to participate and total student-hours to grow faster than annual expenditure. Sustained intensive capacity grows to a viable level and is then protected as the high-touch layer of the portfolio.

At business-as-usual steady state, recurring investment sustains, refreshes and selectively expands the portfolio rather than recreating it from scratch. Alongside curriculum-embedded opportunity growth through 2.1.4, this gives King’s Edge a direct mechanism for creating the additional experiences students need rather than relying only on existing provision.
